items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: there was a fellow on violin named Will Tyler, marvelous violinist... Will Tyler was right with me on each one of my songs.

ctx.x:
Vodery, I don't remember him having.

But anyway, Bill Vodery, he looked at me in the eye, smiling and going on, so I laid him out in the meantime before I went on the stage because, you know. So he -- I told him -- and meantime, there was a fellow on violin named Will Tyler, marvelous violinist. And he heard me tell Bill Vodery to play choruses, no verse, just to play short introduction, four bar introduction, and two choruses of my first song. And just to play four bars and two bars of the next song. Instead he…

Well, Vodery had -- Tyler had heard me, what I said, and while Vodery was playing on this introduction, Will Tyler was playing what I had asked him to play, and I went on and sang what I had asked him to play, you know. And so anyhow, in the meantime, they told me to come back. Now, Will Vodery is going to still do that same trick on me my opening night. The night I'm supposed to open will still play eight bars, and Tyler, the violinist, was going to help me and play the four bars like I told him.
